
# Purpose

Step 3 of the clean donor-level pseudobulk analysis. Takes the 801 cells from
step 2 and:

1. adds draw-to-processing time per donor, and
2. normalizes **for visualization only** to inspect cell-level structure
   (PCA / UMAP), particularly whether processing time drives it.

Raw counts pass through untouched --- step 4 hands DESeq2 raw integers. The
normalization here exists solely to make the embeddings meaningful.

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(uwot)      # UMAP
```

# Parameters

```{r params}
## --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
## All pipeline inputs live in inputs/ (see inputs/README.md for provenance).
INPUT_DIR <- "inputs"
DRAW_XLSX <- file.path(INPUT_DIR, "P635_draw_processed.xlsx")

STEP2_RDS <- file.path("pseudobulk_clean_output", "step2_cells_chains.rds")
OUT_DIR   <- "pseudobulk_clean_output"
FIG_DIR   <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "figures")

## --- Processing time --------------------------------------------------------
TIME_BINARY_CUT <- 6     # hours; < cut => 0 ("fast"), >= cut => 1 ("slow")

## --- Visualization-only normalization ---------------------------------------
VIZ_MIN_CPM      <- 1    # gene kept if CPM > this in >= VIZ_MIN_FRAC of libraries
VIZ_MIN_FRAC     <- 0.10
VIZ_EXCLUDE_IG   <- TRUE # Ig V/D/J/C genes otherwise dominate PC1 by isotype
VIZ_N_HVG        <- 2000
VIZ_N_PCS        <- 20
UMAP_N_NEIGHBORS <- 20
UMAP_MIN_DIST    <- 0.3

GROUP_COLORS <- c(TC = "blue", DS = "red")
SEED         <- 42

set.seed(SEED)
for (d in c(OUT_DIR, FIG_DIR)) dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Load step 2

```{r load_step2}
step2     <- readRDS(STEP2_RDS)
rawCounts <- step2$counts
cells     <- step2$cellAnno
geneAnno  <- step2$geneAnno

cat(sprintf("step 2: %d genes x %d cells\n", nrow(rawCounts), ncol(rawCounts)))
```

# Draw-to-processing time

Per-donor draw and processing timestamps. `TimeElapsed` is hours from draw to
processing; `TimeElapsed_binary` splits at `TIME_BINARY_CUT` hours, matching the
covariate the prior analyst used in her final MAST re-run.

```{r processing_time}
timeToProcess <- read_excel(DRAW_XLSX) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    DrawDateTime      = as.POSIXct(paste(`Draw Date`, `Draw time`),
                                   format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", tz = "UTC"),
    ProcessedDateTime = as.POSIXct(paste(`Date Processed`, `Time Processed`),
                                   format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", tz = "UTC"),
    TimeElapsed        = as.numeric(difftime(ProcessedDateTime, DrawDateTime, units = "hours")),
    TimeElapsed_binary = as.integer(TimeElapsed >= TIME_BINARY_CUT)) %>%
  dplyr::select(donorId, DrawDateTime, ProcessedDateTime, TimeElapsed, TimeElapsed_binary)

stopifnot(!any(is.na(timeToProcess$TimeElapsed)))

cells <- cells %>% dplyr::left_join(timeToProcess, by = "donorId")

## Every donor must get a time, or the covariate is unusable downstream.
missingTime <- cells %>% dplyr::filter(is.na(TimeElapsed)) %>% dplyr::distinct(donorId)
if (nrow(missingTime)) {
  warning("donors without processing time: ", paste(missingTime$donorId, collapse = ", "))
} else cat("all donors matched to a processing time\n")

cells %>%
  dplyr::group_by(studyGroup, project, donorId) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(nCells = dplyr::n(), TimeElapsed = dplyr::first(TimeElapsed),
                   TimeElapsed_binary = dplyr::first(TimeElapsed_binary), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(TimeElapsed) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TimeElapsed = round(TimeElapsed, 1)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Draw-to-processing time per donor")

## Is processing time confounded with study group? This matters for step 3.
tt <- t.test(TimeElapsed ~ studyGroup,
             data = cells %>% dplyr::distinct(donorId, studyGroup, TimeElapsed))
cat(sprintf("\ndonor-level processing time: Ctrl %.1f h vs DS %.1f h (t-test p = %.3f)\n",
            tt$estimate[1], tt$estimate[2], tt$p.value))
print(with(cells %>% dplyr::distinct(donorId, studyGroup, TimeElapsed_binary),
           table(studyGroup, TimeElapsed_binary)))

## Fisher test on the group x fast/slow imbalance.
print(fisher.test(with(cells %>% dplyr::distinct(donorId, studyGroup, TimeElapsed_binary),
                       table(studyGroup, TimeElapsed_binary))))
```

Two features of this variable are worth noting before using it as a covariate:

- **It is bimodal, not continuous.** With the default data the donors split into
  4 processed in 2.0--5.4 h and 12 processed in 18.0--25.9 h, with nothing in
  between. That is same-day versus overnight processing, so the 6 h cut sits in a
  natural gap rather than slicing a continuum --- which makes
  `TimeElapsed_binary` the better-behaved parameterization of the two.
- **It is imbalanced across groups**, 3 Ctrl vs 1 DS in the fast bin. The Fisher
  test above is not significant, but with 16 donors it has almost no power, and
  the imbalance means a processing-time covariate will absorb some genuine
  group signal. There is no way around this in the design: time is a
  donor-level variable, so donor, group and processing time are partly
  collinear (note `donorId` explains slightly more of PC2 than time does).
  Adjusting is still the right call --- it makes the DE estimates conservative
  rather than optimistic --- but the covariate should be reported, not hidden.

# Normalization for visualization

Raw counts stay raw for step 3. Here we build a separate log-CPM matrix purely
to look at cell-level structure. Ig V/D/J/C genes are excluded by default ---
otherwise the leading component simply separates isotypes and hides everything
else.

```{r normalize_viz}
countsViz <- rawCounts[, cells$libid]

keepGene <- rowMeans(edgeR::cpm(countsViz) > VIZ_MIN_CPM) >= VIZ_MIN_FRAC
if (VIZ_EXCLUDE_IG) {
  igGenes  <- geneAnno$ensgene[geneAnno$isIg]
  keepGene <- keepGene & !(rownames(countsViz) %in% igGenes)
}
countsViz <- countsViz[keepGene, ]
logCPM <- log2(edgeR::cpm(countsViz) + 1)

## Highly variable genes, then PCA on centred (not scaled) log-CPM.
geneVar <- matrixStats::rowVars(logCPM)
hvg     <- names(sort(geneVar, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(VIZ_N_HVG, length(geneVar)))]
pca     <- prcomp(t(logCPM[hvg, ]), center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
pctVar  <- 100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)

cat(sprintf("%d genes pass the expression filter, %d HVGs used for PCA\n",
            nrow(countsViz), length(hvg)))
cat(sprintf("variance explained: PC1 %.1f%%, PC2 %.1f%%, PC3 %.1f%%\n",
            pctVar[1], pctVar[2], pctVar[3]))

umap <- uwot::umap(pca$x[, seq_len(VIZ_N_PCS)], n_neighbors = UMAP_N_NEIGHBORS,
                   min_dist = UMAP_MIN_DIST, seed = SEED)

## Keep the first five PCs for the association table below.
viz <- dplyr::bind_cols(
  cells,
  as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:5]) %>% setNames(paste0("PC", 1:5)),
  tibble(UMAP1 = umap[, 1], UMAP2 = umap[, 2]))
```

## What drives the leading components?

Variance in each PC explained by candidate drivers, so the plots below can be
read quantitatively rather than by eye.

```{r pc_associations}
drivers <- c("TimeElapsed", "TimeElapsed_binary", "studyGroup", "isotype",
             "donorId", "libSize", "nGenes", "pctMito", "pctRibo", "plate")
do.call(rbind, lapply(paste0("PC", 1:5), function(pc)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(drivers, function(dv) {
    if (!dv %in% names(viz) || dplyr::n_distinct(viz[[dv]], na.rm = TRUE) < 2)
      return(NULL)
    fit <- lm(reformulate(dv, response = pc), data = viz)
    data.frame(PC = pc, driver = dv,
               R2 = round(summary(fit)$r.squared, 3),
               p = signif(anova(fit)[dv, "Pr(>F)"], 3))
  })))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PC, values_from = c(R2, p)) %>%
  dplyr::select(driver, dplyr::starts_with("R2"), dplyr::starts_with("p_")) %>%
  kable(caption = "Variance explained (R2) and ANOVA p per PC")
```

## PCA and UMAP

```{r viz_plots, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.4}
plotEmbedding <- function(dat, colourBy, title = colourBy) {
  pcaPlot <- ggplot(dat, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = .data[[colourBy]])) +
    geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", pctVar[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", pctVar[2]),
         colour = NULL, title = paste("PCA:", title)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11)
  umapPlot <- ggplot(dat, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = .data[[colourBy]])) +
    geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(colour = NULL, title = paste("UMAP:", title)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11)
  if (is.numeric(dat[[colourBy]])) {
    pcaPlot  <- pcaPlot  + scale_colour_viridis_c()
    umapPlot <- umapPlot + scale_colour_viridis_c()
  }
  print(pcaPlot); print(umapPlot)
}

plotEmbedding(viz, "TimeElapsed", "hours from draw to processing")
plotEmbedding(viz %>% dplyr::mutate(TimeElapsed_binary = factor(TimeElapsed_binary)),
              "TimeElapsed_binary", sprintf("processing time >= %d h", TIME_BINARY_CUT))
plotEmbedding(viz, "studyGroup")
plotEmbedding(viz %>% dplyr::mutate(isotype = tidyr::replace_na(isotype, "none")), "isotype")
plotEmbedding(viz, "project", "donor")
plotEmbedding(viz, "nGenes", "genes detected")
```

## Reading these plots

With the default parameters the structure is unambiguous, and it matters for
step 3:

- **PC1 is sequencing depth**, not biology: `nGenes` explains ~83% of it
  (isotype ~31%). Expected for full-length plate data and handled by
  normalization in the DE model.
- **PC2 is draw-to-processing time.** `TimeElapsed_binary` explains ~79% of PC2
  and continuous `TimeElapsed` ~68%; the fast-processed donors form a visually
  distinct band. This is the largest non-depth axis in the data.
- **Study group shares that axis** (~18% of PC2). Processing time is therefore
  partly confounded with DS vs Ctrl at the cell level, even though the
  donor-level means are not significantly different (see the t-test above; with
  only 16 donors that test has little power, so a non-significant result is not
  reassurance).
- **PC3 is isotype** (~40%), which is the biology the pseudobulk comparison
  conditions on by analysing IgG and IgM separately.

Practical consequence: include `TimeElapsed_binary` in the step 3 design. This
also explains a result from the earlier audit --- HBB and HBA2, the strongest
"DEGs" in the published cell-level analysis, are erythrocyte-contamination genes
whose apparent DS-vs-Ctrl signal weakens once processing time is adjusted for.


# Save for step 4

```{r save}
countsStep3 <- rawCounts[, cells$libid]
stopifnot(all(countsStep3 %% 1 == 0), identical(colnames(countsStep3), cells$libid))

saveRDS(list(counts = countsStep3, cellAnno = cells, geneAnno = geneAnno,
             viz = viz %>% dplyr::select(libid, PC1:PC5, UMAP1, UMAP2),
             pctVar = pctVar,
             params = list(TIME_BINARY_CUT = TIME_BINARY_CUT,
                           VIZ_EXCLUDE_IG = VIZ_EXCLUDE_IG, SEED = SEED),
             sessionInfo = sessionInfo()),
        file.path(OUT_DIR, "step3_cells_time_structure.rds"))
write_csv(cells, file.path(OUT_DIR, "step3_cell_metadata.csv"))

cat(sprintf("saved %d genes x %d cells (raw counts) to %s\n",
            nrow(countsStep3), ncol(countsStep3),
            file.path(OUT_DIR, "step3_cells_time_structure.rds")))

## Cells available per donor x isotype -- this sets pseudobulk power in step 4.
cells %>%
  dplyr::filter(isotype %in% c("IGHG", "IGHM")) %>%
  dplyr::count(studyGroup, project, isotype) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = isotype, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(studyGroup, project) %>%
  kable(caption = "Cells per donor for the IgG / IgM pseudobulk comparison")
```

# Where this goes next

Step 4 pseudobulks these raw counts by donor x isotype and runs DESeq2 and
limma with `~ studyGroup + TimeElapsed_binary`.
